summary.headline: Shriram Finance Q1 FY27 PAT rose 59.79% YoY to ₹3,444.56 crore, with NIM at 9.04% and AUM up 15.26% YoY to ₹3,13,798 crore.
summary.overview: Q1 FY27 disbursements grew 19.51% YoY to ₹49,974 crore and AUM reached ₹3,13,798 crore, up 3.81% QoQ. Net interest income rose 33.67% YoY to ₹8,055.70 crore and NIM widened to 9.04%, helped by surplus liquidity from the April 2026 capital infusion. Borrowings were reduced, leverage fell to 2.14x from 3.82x in March, and gross stage 3 edged up to 4.64%. Management kept the FY27 AUM growth guidance of 18% and said the surplus liquidity will be deployed into growth rather than debt repayment.

segments.name: Passenger vehicles (disbursement)
segments.commentary: Disbursed ₹11,018 crore in Q1 FY27 per the call's breakdown.

segments.name: Commercial vehicles / used and new CV
segments.commentary: Management said CV sales rose nearly 20%, with used-vehicle demand healthy in rural markets; the new-vehicle share of the portfolio is rising slowly.

segments.name: MSME
segments.commentary: Disbursed ₹6,184 crore in Q1 FY27; management expects MSME to reach about 20% of the book and needs ₹7,000 crore+ quarterly disbursements from Q3 FY27 to accelerate growth.

segments.name: Construction equipment
segments.commentary: Disbursed ₹792 crore in Q1 FY27, well below the ~₹2,000 crore run rate of FY25; management cited some demand recovery.

segments.name: Two-wheelers and personal loans
segments.commentary: Disbursed ₹3,548 crore (two-wheelers) and ₹2,773 crore (personal loans); farm equipment ₹947 crore.

guidance_outlook: FY27 AEM growth guidance of 18% retained; management expects at least 15% growth in Q2 FY27 and will reassess after Q2.
Operating NIM expected to settle around 8.5% as surplus liquidity benefit fades; analysts questioned this given the current 9.04%.
Cost to income ratio guided to remain stable.

No further liability repayments; surplus liquidity (about ₹7,000-18,000 crore buffer retained) to be deployed into growth, with excess liquidity used over one to one and a half months; fresh borrowing planned towards end of Q2, likely including securitisation.
Incremental borrowing cost expected around 8% from banks, below the 8.56% average cost of liabilities.
Around 150 new branches planned for FY27; MSME growth expected to exceed the overall book growth, with CV growth around 15%.
Credit cost guidance of below 2% retained for the near term.
capex_capacity: Around 150 branches tentatively planned for FY27 to support growth.
Liquidity coverage ratio at 462.54%; buffer of roughly three months of future liability repayments (₹7,000-18,000 crore) maintained.
demand_pricing: Vehicle sales strong: passenger vehicle sales rose about 20% YoY per management, and CV sales grew nearly 20%; the used-vehicle segment is seeing good rural demand.
Lower borrowing costs are being passed on to new-vehicle buyers, which management said will weigh on margins on new vehicle loans.
Gold loan growth continued; management said there is no asset quality pressure in gold or MSME, and that retail fuel price pass-through to manufacturers was a one-time cost increase.
Off-balance-sheet share of AUM has declined over recent quarters because no securitisation or direct assignment deals were done in Q1 FY27; securitisation is expected towards quarter-end.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the 9.04% NIM comes from surplus liquidity, and will it hold?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the liquidity from the recent equity infusion added about ₹500 crore of interest income in the quarter; operating NIM is expected to hold near 8.5% and the liquidity benefit to subside over time.

qa_highlights.question: Why is guidance for NIM at 8.5% when current NIM is 9% with surplus liquidity?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said lower cost of borrowing is being passed on to new-vehicle buyers and the mix is shifting; no detailed bridge was given beyond that.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company raise fresh borrowing given surplus liquidity?
qa_highlights.answer: No further repayments; surplus liquidity will be used for growth over one to one and a half months, and fresh borrowing is planned for the end of the quarter, including securitisation.

qa_highlights.question: Any asset quality impact from the monsoon or the crisis?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there is no sign of demand destruction so far and vehicle sales are up about 20% YoY; gold and MSME asset quality is fine, with MSME caution applied over the last year.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the CV growth and will it continue?
qa_highlights.answer: CV sales up nearly 20%; the rural used-vehicle demand is good; management is comfortable with growth and is not pushing extra; CV growth projected around 15%.

qa_highlights.question: Is the MSME business recovering?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said MSME growth will be higher than the overall book growth and disbursements need to rise to ₹7,000 crore+ from Q3 FY27.

risks_watch: Monsoon uncertainty and West Asia crisis could affect disbursements in Q2 FY27; the company said Q2 is typically tricky.
Stage 3 rose on a QoQ basis in CV, and management called the increase marginal.
Margin sustainability: NIM guided to decline toward 8.5% as liquidity benefit fades; the 9.04% level is partly one-time.
Funding environment: planned fresh borrowing late in the quarter, with incremental cost near 8%.
Construction equipment disbursements have stayed near ₹1,000 crore for five quarters.
summary.management_tone: Confident on growth, asset quality and funding, but evasive on the NIM path. Management stated outright that growth would pick up, yet gave little bridge for the decline to 8.5%.
key_quotes: Our earlier guidance of 18% will hold good unless you know after second quarter we revise it.
So one time increase in cost is already passed on and people have started living with it and therefore I think there's there may not be further surprise.
Yeah, in fact, previously we used to borrow as a double-rated entity and now we are getting the benefit of rating that itself uses some benefit of lower cost.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management will reassess FY27 guidance only after Q2, and the 18% AUM target is held rather than raised; no upgrade was signalled.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade

rows.label: Fresh borrowing and securitisation at quarter-end

rows.label: Leverage down to 2.14x
rows.why: Leverage fell to 2.14x from 3.82x in March and total liabilities dropped to ₹2,32,639 crore from ₹2,50,690 crore, with no further repayments planned.
